speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, how long have you been experiencing the increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, and does the pain seem to come and go in attacks?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome). The presentation of asymmetric oligoarthritis affecting the lower extremities (left ankle, now right knee) combined with urethritis (pain with urination) and a history of inconsistent condom use is highly characteristic of Reactive Arthritis, often triggered by a sexually transmitted infection or gastrointestinal pathogen. The family history of rheumatoid arthritis is likely incidental.
